newsitem.title: DUBAI: Politics is no obstacle to UAE-Iran trade, official.
newsitem.headline: Politics is no obstacle to UAE-Iran trade, official.

text.p: Trade between Dubai and its non-Arab Gulf neighbour Iran will not be affected by political differences between the two countries, a United Arab Emirates official said.

"Political differences with Iran are marginal when it comes to economic relations," said Abdulrahman Al-Mutawii, director general of Dubai's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, as quoted by the daily Al-Khaleej on Wednesday.

"It's a neighbouring Moslem country and there are direct trade links," he said, according to Al-Khaleej. "Iran is Dubai's leading trade partner since the seventies and we have strong neighbourly relations."
One thorny issue in Iran's relations with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states is a territorial dispute with the UAE over three Gulf islands.

Earlier this year, the GCC -- which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain and Oman -- accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs and expressed worries over its rearmament programme. Iran denied the charges.

Dubai, the trading hub of the UAE, is Iran's main link to foreign goods, particularly foreign machinery, mechanical appliances and electrical equipment, according to the Dubai Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
Customs department figures show the value of re-export trade between Dubai and Iran reached 2.99 billion dirhams ($815 million) in the period from January-November 1995.
